key_insight: Evolution Strategy trained directly on a large turbulent channel learns a recurrent wall controller that avoids small-box degeneracies and cuts skin-friction drag by about 26%.
engineering_relevance: This suggests gradient-free closed-loop control can scale better than prior MARL policies for practical turbulent drag-reduction designs in larger domains.
method: Optimize a recurrent controller with Evolution Strategy instead of backpropagation.
Evaluate candidate policies over full flow episodes using an energy-aware objective.
Train and test directly in a large channel at Re_tau ≃ 180 with parallel policy evaluation.
evidence_signal: The ES controller reduced drag by about 26%, outperforming GRU-MARL trained on a minimal box (17%) and slightly exceeding classic opposition control (22%).
watch_item: Performance depends on full-episode, large-domain evaluation, so controllers trained in smaller periodic boxes may not transfer reliably and can still be sensitive to actuation degeneracies.
paper_title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction
